The recommended quality control procedures for sanitized AK23 consist of immunoblot analysis, SDS‐PAGE, the keratinocyte dissociation assay (KDA), and mouse passive transfer. These protocols are described in detail in the related article describing reproducible AK23 production (Müller et al., 2024). If the ETX purification procedure (Basic Protocols 1 and 2) is performed on AK23 IgG isolated from AK23 hybridoma supernatants, these quality control steps are recommended. If the ETX purification is done with already isolated AK23 IgG, controls should include validation of the functional activity of AK23 before and after sanitization using a KDA on primary human or mouse keratinocytes (Fig. 4A shows primary human keratinocytes; the method is described in detail in Müller et al., 2024). Furthermore, AK23 binding efficiency to primary human or mouse keratinocytes before and after sanitization should be tested by direct immunofluorescence (Fig. 4B shows primary human keratinocytes) as described in the protocol below.

NOTE: It is important to perform direct immunofluorescence staining with AK23 IgG under high‐calcium conditions without fixation and at 4°C, as AK23 does not bind to fixed cells or under low‐calcium conditions, and the low temperature prevents its internalization.

steps.title: Prepare endotoxin‑free solutions
steps.instruction: Make all buffers with water for injection (WFI) and verify each solution for low‑level endotoxin (<0.2 EU/ml) before use.

steps.title: Sanitize glassware, system, and resin
steps.instruction: Flush glassware, the ÄKTA Avant (or equivalent) chromatography system, and the Protein A column with 0.5 M NaOH (Merck Supelco, cat. no. 1.09138.1000) for the recommended contact time, then rinse thoroughly with WFI.

steps.title: Verify endotoxin levels in devices
steps.instruction: Test the rinsed devices and all prepared buffers using either the Endosafe Nexgen‑MSC benchtop LAL assay (Fisher Scientific, cat. no. 19121107/1) with Compendial cartridges (0.1 EU, 10 EU per pack, cat. no. NC9667085) or the clotting‑based LAL test (Lonza, cat. no. N283‑06).

steps.title: Bind AK23 IgG to Protein A column
steps.instruction: Load purified AK23 IgG (or hybridoma supernatant containing AK23, PV IgG, or control antibodies) onto the sanitized 5 ml MabSelect Protein A HiTrap column (Cytiva, cat. no. GE17‑0403‑01) equilibrated with PBS, pH 7.4 (<0.2 EU/ml ETX). Allow binding at the recommended flow rate.

steps.title: Strip endotoxin on‑column with arginine
steps.instruction: Pass 0.5 M arginine (Fisher Scientific, cat. no. A14730.36) prepared in PBS, pH 7.4 (<0.5 EU/ml ETX) through the IgG‑bound column to unfold IgG‑ETX complexes.

substeps.instruction: Wash column with 0.5 M arginine solution at the same flow rate used for binding.
Rinse column with PBS, pH 7.4 (<0.2 EU/ml ETX) to remove residual arginine.
Optional: flush with 70 % (v/v) ethanol (prepared from absolute ethanol, Merck Supelco, cat. no. 1.00983) to further reduce endotoxin, then rinse again with PBS.

steps.title: Elute IgG and neutralize
steps.instruction: Elute the IgG from the column with 0.1 M glycine, pH 3.0 (Merck, cat. no. 50046‑250g) and immediately neutralize each fraction with 0.1 M Tris‑Cl, pH 8.0 (Merck, cat. no. T1503‑100g).

substeps.instruction: Collect eluate fractions into tubes kept on ice.
Add an equal volume of 0.1 M Tris‑Cl to each fraction to bring pH to ~7.5.

steps.title: Concentrate and buffer‑exchange IgG
steps.instruction: Transfer the neutralized eluate to a 20‑ml Vivaspin20 ultrafiltration device (MWCO 3000, Cytiva, cat. no. 28932358) and spin at the recommended speed until the desired concentration is reached, then diafilter into endotoxin‑free PBS, pH 7.4.

steps.title: Quantify endotoxin in purified IgG
steps.instruction: Measure endotoxin in the final IgG preparation with the Endosafe Nexgen‑MSC benchtop LAL test using Compendial cartridges, confirming <0.5 EU/ml (or the specific in‑process limits listed in Table 1).

steps.title: Perform immunofluorescence binding assay
steps.instruction: Assess AK23 binding to primary human (or mouse) keratinocytes before and after sanitization under high‑calcium, non‑fixed conditions at 4 °C.

substeps.instruction: Culture primary human epidermal keratinocyte progenitor (HPEK) cells in CnT‑NX‑EX medium supplemented with 226 mM CaCl₂ stock solution; incubate at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂, 90 % humidity.
Detach cells onto 8‑well removable chambered glass slides (ibidi, cat. no. 80841) and keep on ice.
Prepare staining buffer: PBS+ with 1 % (v/v) BSA, kept ice‑cold.
Add AK23 IgG (pre‑ and post‑sanitization) at 1–20 µg/ml in the high‑calcium buffer; incubate 30 min at 4 °C.
Add goat anti‑mouse IgG (H+L) Alexa Fluor 594 secondary antibody (Invitrogen, cat. no. A‑11005) diluted in PBS+; incubate 30 min at 4 °C in the dark.
Stain nuclei with 1 mg/ml Hoechst 33342 (AAT BioQuest, cat. no. 17530) for 5 min at room temperature.
Mount slides with fluorescence mounting medium (Dako, cat. no. S302380‑2) and image using a fluorescence microscope (Nikon Eclipse Ti‑E).

steps.title: Additional quality controls
steps.instruction: Confirm IgG purity by SDS‑PAGE and activity by keratinocyte dissociation assay (KDA) as described in Müller et al. (2024); use mIgG1 control (BioXCell, cat. no. BE0083, ≤0.05 EU/mg) for comparison.
